This is  acute little ghost game. Calling it a "horror game" would be a bit of a stretch but it does have some scary scenes and jump scares. It is essentially a parody of the trope in which you live in a cursed apartment with a ghost that is trying to harm you.
The titular ghost is a clear copy from Sadakos text book, long black hair that covers most of the face, a white dress and pale skin. She is designed to look less horrific and more in the area of a cute ghost girl though. They even copied the seven day cycle in which Sadakos curse hits you but in this case its you living in an apartment for seven days before it gets teared down.
You encounter the ghost very early and she tries to scare you but the protagonist is really dense or does nnot really care abot ghosts, anyway, the ghost fails hard to scare you, so instead she tries to be as annoying as possible towards you, stealing your food and playing tricks on you.
The gameplay is rather shallow but it's at least not a pure walking simulator. Each day you have some sort of objective, usually finding some items or solving a small puzzle. While you look for items, you have to be aware of the ghost. She tries to "sneak" up on you to scare you (which resets the day) but you can hear hear coming thanks to hear scare chord. If you turn around, she will freeze in her motion and disappear. This is essentially similiar to the Weeping Angels in Doctor Who, as long as you are looking at the ghost, even while she is invisible, she will not move. This can help to move around the apartment but if you look at her too often she will teleport to another place and since she is invisible when you look at her, you don't know exactly when it happens.
The gameplay is okay as it is, it can become sometimes annoying when you try to figure out the solution to a puzzle but are not allowed to look at it because the ghost is behind you. I also noticed that she becomes more aggressive/faster as more days go on but maybe that's just my imagination.

The game has a good hint system, if you struggle too long with a puzzle, generally when you are looking for an item, the game will send you a text message on your phone, giving you a hint where to look. The game is overall not too hard, the puzzles are easy and the only challenge is not to get caught by the ghost, which is also easy to manage since she is so god damn loud.
Overall I would rate the game more for the story than the actual gameplay, it's  a cute ghost story with a rather incompetent but adorable ghost girl who tries her best to become a menance to the guy that has entered her apartment. Over the seven day time span you interact with the ghost, get to know each other better and learn to live with each other. For it's short time the game also has two different endings. Each day has a hidden seal somehwere in the apartment and you need to find them all if you want the alternate ending. It's a short experience, something that you can probably finish in two hours if you solve the puzzles quickly but it was funny enough for me to not care that much.

I usually buy games in bundles or at deep discounts but this thing was different. I saw the gameplay (The ‘stag beetle’ part got me. I absolutely adore the megasoma. The Polish name for rhinoceros beetle is ‘rohatyniec nosorożec’ and I think that’s beautiful) and decided this game may be too unique to just watch. Plus, I’m old enough now to buy horror games on a whim, on Sunday, 15 minutes to midnight. 

The first puzzle was getting the game started since it launches in Japanese. I’ve managed since it only has two items inside the options menu: language and fullscreen setting. Also, the windowed option proved unplayable on my computer. The game offered no way of changing the window resolution, so the game still covered the entire screen only now with the title bar saying ‘Project Shiawase’ displayed on top. Right next to the Unity icon. I admired the diligence with which Seven managed to inform me that the game was running on Unity about three times before I even got to start playing.   

[h3]I don’t look like a, uh… ghost, do I? [/h3]

The gameplay is extremely basic. Each day, the player is given a list of objects to find around the apartment where the protagonist is staying. At the same time, the ghost randomly spawns and homes in slowly on the player. There is a high pitch sound informing the player that they are being followed and if they manage to look at the ghost before it reaches them, it disappears. Then, the entire chase sequence starts over until the player is either caught or able to complete the objectives. After that there is a short cinematic, followed by a screen saying “Mission Complete” (sorely lacking the Metal Gear Solid VR mission fanfare). Finally, the player is treated to another ‘Made with Unity’ screen and kicked back to the main menu where they need to start another day manually. There is no saving option available but with each ‘mission’ being only a few minutes long there is no need for one. 

[h3]See? I’m real. [/h3]

It takes less than 2 hours to finish this game for the first time and unlock every achievement. It’s not a long story and it would probably take about 20 minutes to complete when the player already knows what to do. The controls are very basic, graphics are unimpressive, and the sound is nearly nonexistent besides the bare minimal effects and three or four songs playing in the background.
 
Furthermore, for such a short game, there is an extensive number of bugs. None of the options work properly: windowed mode is broken, the English translation is poor (but in a  charming way –  outside of chapter 6 when the game gives player the instructions on what to do next in a form of a riddle and the quality of translation makes it frustrating) and there’s also a mouse sensitivity slider, but it only appears when the player views the options during the game and not from the main menu.  Once or twice, I had the ghost spawn so close to the protagonist that it resulted in an instant chapter restart, and sometimes the chime that is supposed to warn the player that the ghost is approaching did not play. Said ghost is animated very sparsely, and even when she does move, her body notoriously clips through her hair which distracts from enjoying the cutscenes. 

[h3]Do I look like your girlfriend? [/h3]

But while at times Seven indeed felt more like a ‘project’ than a proper game, it did not change the fact that the main gameplay loop is enjoyable. There is a perfect mixture of humor, tension and charm involved. 

There are two endings. Unexpectedly for a ghost story, both may be classified as happy ones in their own ways. On a philosophical ground, I might contest the claim that the best possible outcome of the Seven’s events would be for the protagonist [spoiler] to spend the rest of his life with a supernatural being that has attempted to kill him before [/spoiler], but that’s probably subjective. Both endings show the player ‘Made with Unity’ screen twice. 

Having said all that, while I cannot wholeheartedly recommend this game, I can’t bring myself to give it a negative review either. For what it offers, both in terms of length and quality, the price is rather steep and there are plenty of more competent games. It’s not a – despite what Steam reviews may tell you – 9 out of 10 game. It’s a strong 6, an acceptable first effort of TozukuGames and as such it deserves an upvote. I just hope their following games would show a decisively more polish since the - pun intended - spirit is already there.

As always, do with this knowledge whatever you will and 
[h3] Try to have a wonderful life. [/h3]

[i]Seven Nights Ghost[/i] is a horror game that's more on the silly/heartwarming side than actually scary. If the "Sexual Content" tag makes or breaks your decision to purchase this, ignore it; there is nothing of the sort in this game.

You play as a man who has temporarily been relocated for work to a housing complex that's going to be demolished pretty much immediately after your stay. Why they would have you stay up until the wire is beyond me, but whatever. Shortly after arriving, you find out that the building referred to as haunted is indeed so... by a ghost who's a little more of a nuisance than an actual threat.

Each night, you need to find objects and sometimes solve puzzles throughout your room while the ghost sneaks up behind you to jumpscare you (according to the page she doesn't kill you, so maybe she's just being a pest). Thankfully she's loud and apparently shy since she will vanish shortly after you look at her. She does become faster and more aggressive as you progress, so be sure to wear headphones to help determine which direction to look, especially since she can spawn right near you and is silent for a second or so.

The game isn't very long and can be completed in a few hours depending on how fast you find everything/solve the puzzles and how often she gets you (take your time to look around when you get to the part where you [spoiler]fix the figurine[/spoiler]).

Overall, I don't regret my experience living with a ghost for seven days, but you may want to wait until this is on sale to check in.

The entity looks like a generic Yūrei (幽霊), which usually depicted as wearing a white long dress or a burial kimono, and long black unkempt hair covering the face. More often look like Sadako from The Ring (1998).

There are many types of it, some of them are:
-Bōrei (亡霊): A type of yūrei that means "ruined" or "departed" spirit. Unrecognizable bodiy shape or face, badly damage.
-Shiryō (死霊): A type of yūrei that means "dead" spirit. Lingers around spots or places where they still have unfinished business.
-Obake (お化け): Another term for yūrei. Often neutral unless provoked.
Onryō (怨霊): A type of yūrei that is intensely vengeful and seeks retribution for a past injustice.

But you can chillax, because there's only one type in this game. And you only have one week to appease this restless spirit.

This game takes a twist to the typical indie horror game. The storytelling gives a bitter sweet experience, where you feel the creeps and anxiety coupled with relief and sweetness. It takes the player through 7 nights to unfold the story, and you'll look forward to the next always. In fact it was over too soon, I wish there were more.

Game experience wise, it hasn't the best graphics, you'll need headphones to play this game efficiently as sounds are crucial. Some cutscenes were too dark to see what happened. I didn't experience any lag, running on 3080 GPU. There are 2 different post-credit endings. For the price-point, it's a fair deal as the puzzles were not blatantly easy that you play through with one eye closed. Visually, the game was bland with uninspired settings and character designs. The company housing, which serves as the primary setting of the game, was devoid of any eerie or mysterious aura that one would expect from a horror setting. The ghost, which could have been the focal point of the game's visual design, was unimaginatively designed. The audio did little to salvage the experience - the background music was monotonous and the sound effects were barely noticeable.

The gameplay was the final nail in the coffin. The exploration aspect of the game, which could have been a saving grace, was stymied by the lack of interactivity and engagement within the environment. The game consisted of navigating through the company housing with little to no challenges, making it feel like a chore rather than an exciting venture into the unknown. Living with the ghost for seven days could have introduced interesting gameplay dynamics, however, it was reduced to mundane and repetitive tasks that did not contribute to the storyline or the gameplay experience.

In conclusion, Seven Nights Ghost is a missed opportunity. The unique blend of a heartwarming narrative within a horror framework could have paved the way for an innovative gaming experience. However, the lackluster plot, bland visual and audio design, and uninspired gameplay make it a forgettable experience. It's a game that promises peaceful days full of curses, but ultimately delivers boring nights full of disappointments.

[list]
    [*]The game defaults to Japanese so you have to hope and pray you hit the right commands to eventually swap languages.

    [*]Some sections are just exhaustingly stretched out like filing the glue down and waiting for your phone to charge. At some points you're just at the mercy of the spawn points and hope rng doesn't make you do the entire day again.
    [*]The whole puzzle day doesn't make a lot of sense. Apparently I wandered around looking for the key and completely forgot I stumbled through most of the puzzles and died previously so I had to redo a section I forgot I stumbled upon the previous life.
    [*]Some items are so randomly placed or used for logic (like the adhesive or the hanger for chopsticks) that this almost feels like a "guide required" sorta joint.
[/list]
